episodesAudited: episodeSelection array entries 7–18 (includes campaign IDs reused from baseline and numbered order field) in docs/design/odysseys/church-of-rome.json
auditType: read-only source-access and claim audit; no repository edits

episodes.place: Rome; the specific refuge points are churches/shrines, not a named lower-Tiber site

sources.kind: primary theological polemic, Augustine, City of God I.1
sources.access: Full relevant chapter accessed via parallel public translation at https://www.logoslibrary.org/augustine/city/0101.html; cited New Advent URL itself not separately opened
sources.locator: Book I, chapter 1
sources.supports: Augustine says apostolic/martyr churches functioned as refuges in the sack for people fleeing, including Christians and pagans; he attributes restraint to the Christian name/sanctuary status.
sources.limits: Written after the event to answer pagan criticism; not an eyewitness incident log. Does not document a lower-Tiber route, household, grain store, or particular rescue.

episodes.assessment: The sanctuary claim is supported as Augustine's argument. Player households, evacuation, supplies and route remain fictional framing.

episodes.place: Ravenna; Italy and the western imperial administration

sources.kind: secondary overview
sources.access: Search result overview accessed; full article not consulted
sources.locator: Fall of the Western Roman Empire overview
sources.supports: Provides conventional event framing for Odoacer's deposition of Romulus Augustulus in 476.
sources.limits: Not primary evidence. No detailed institutional claim verified from this page.

sources.kind: late antique chronicle (Marcellinus Comes, entry for 476)
sources.access: Displayed Latin and English translation read
sources.locator: Chronicon, 476 entry
sources.supports: Calls Odoacer king and says the western empire perished with Augustulus, an explicit retrospective interpretation.
sources.limits: Chronicle was composed decades later from an eastern imperial perspective. Does not show that contemporaries viewed 476 as a sudden end of Roman institutions; episode itself correctly cautions against claiming Rome/church ended.

episodes.assessment: The date is a political marker; do not narrate an instantaneous end of Roman ecclesiastical or civic administration. No institutional primary record was consulted here.

episodes.place: Ravenna; Theoderic's entry into the palace/Lauretum in the Valesian account

sources.kind: late antique narrative, Anonymus Valesianus, pars posterior
sources.access: Latin and English rendering of §§54–57 read
sources.supports: The account says Theoderic entered Ravenna; after several days he personally killed Odoacer, and Odoacer's army and family were killed by order. The Goths then confirmed Theoderic as king.
sources.limits: Retrospective narrative with political/characterizing language; it gives no securely established exact day in the passage consulted, and one source cannot support exact civilian impact or an extraction operation.

episodes.assessment: Core succession event supported. Do not conflate this with Theoderic's later visit to Rome in 500. No named civilian rescue is evidenced.

episodes.date: 494 CE (letter commonly dated 494; exact dating may be expressed as c.494)
episodes.place: Rome to Emperor Anastasius I; diplomatic exchange involving envoys returning from Constantinople

sources.kind: full translation of primary letter, Gelasius I, Famuli vestrae pietatis
sources.access: Full translation and contextual introduction read
sources.locator: Letter opening and argument on duo sunt / priestly authority and imperial power
sources.supports: Gelasius addresses Anastasius and argues for distinct sacred authority of bishops and royal power; introductory context says the letter responds to a diplomatic exchange involving returning envoys.
sources.limits: A situated papal argument and advocacy, not a neutral constitutional compact or timeless settlement. This modern translation page itself notes its collaborative translation; no license for reuse of text/image assets established.

episodes.assessment: Supports a contemporary argument about responsibilities, not a definitive settlement of church-state relations.

episodes.place: Constantinople; negotiations between the Roman see, Emperor Justin I and the Constantinopolitan patriarchate

sources.kind: primary profession/formula associated with Hormisdas, translated from OCR-derived source
sources.access: Formula translation and subscription passage read; page labels translation AI-assisted and gives original Latin/Greek availability
sources.locator: Libellus text, closing subscription
sources.supports: The profession accepts communion articulated by the apostolic see and promises not to commemorate those separated from it; the document's text supports a formal ecclesial settlement effort.
sources.limits: Translation is explicitly AI-assisted/OCR-derived, so exact wording should be checked against an edition before quoting. Formula alone does not prove every church accepted it or that all doctrinal/jurisdictional conflicts ended.

sources.kind: older secondary reference, Catholic Encyclopedia entry on Acacian Schism
sources.access: Search-result description and supplied episode locator only; full page not read in this audit
sources.locator: Acacian Schism / 519 reconciliation
sources.supports: Secondary overview labels the 519 settlement as end of the schism.
sources.limits: Older confessional reference; not a primary source and not evidence that all divisions disappeared.

episodes.assessment: A reconciliation in 519 is supported as an institutional event, but phrase it as ending the Acacian schism/formal communion dispute, not as universal doctrinal consensus.

episodes.date: Embassy dispatched late 525 or early 526; John's death at Ravenna 18 May 526 in standard chronology
episodes.place: Constantinople (embassy destination), then Ravenna (arrest/death); the dispatch began at Theodoric's court

sources.kind: later papal biography, Liber Pontificalis, life of John I
sources.access: Search-result excerpt only; not full passage read
sources.locator: John I biography / embassy to Constantinople
sources.supports: Excerpt describes John and senators arriving in Constantinople and being received by the people; later biography is a source for the mission tradition.
sources.limits: Search excerpt only; the Liber Pontificalis is later and its redactions differ.

sources.kind: institutional biographical reference, Treccani
sources.access: Search excerpt only
sources.locator: Embassy and imprisonment chronology
sources.supports: Dates the embassy around late 525/early 526 and reports John's arrest after return and death in Ravenna.
sources.limits: Secondary synthesis; source traditions on the exact dispatch date and Theodoric's motive are disputed/mediated.

sources.kind: institutional papal biography, Treccani
sources.access: Search excerpt only
sources.locator: John I, embassy chronology
sources.supports: Notes that timing differs among sources and that Liber Pontificalis and Anonymus Valesianus reflect distinct political perspectives.
sources.limits: Excerpt only; no definitive precise departure date established.

episodes.assessment: Embassy and imprisonment narrative should be attributed to later accounts. Do not claim motives as objective fact; date range properly remains qualified.

episodes.date: 536 CE; Rome's entry usually dated 9 December in modern chronology
episodes.place: Rome; Procopius narrates the army entering the city after the Gothic garrison withdraws

sources.kind: primary narrative, Procopius, Wars V (Gothic War I)
sources.access: Full online translation accessed; search/index and narrative passage consulted
sources.locator: Book V, chapter 14, especially §14; index identifies Belisarius' entry into Rome
sources.supports: Procopius describes Belisarius' forces taking possession of Rome after the Goths left; a letter attributed to Belisarius reports taking Rome.
sources.limits: Procopius served with Belisarius and writes from the imperial side. Does not verify episode's fictional district supply/occupation tasks or exact local civilian logistics.

episodes.assessment: Core entry event supported; keep the map local to Rome and identify the relief/supply tasks as fictional.

episodes.date: 537–538 CE; Procopius says the siege began March 1 and lasted until about a year later
episodes.place: Rome and its circuit walls; supplies/harbor details include Portus/Ostia

sources.kind: primary narrative, Procopius, Wars V–VI
sources.access: Full online translation accessed; relevant siege chronology and narrative read
sources.locator: Book V, siege narrative, esp. XXIV; index entries for siege/relief
sources.supports: Procopius states that Rome's first siege by Vitiges continued for about a year, with famine/blocked necessities and attempts at relief. He describes grain/provisions moving by land and sea in the broader account.
sources.limits: Narrative is shaped by imperial perspective and uses dramatic/large numbers; do not reuse its army counts as reliable exact totals. Episode's exact day counts should remain qualified.

episodes.assessment: The siege and relief context is well supported; no specific fictional civilian withdrawal or supply cache is attested.

episodes.date: 546 CE (Totila's capture during siege); reported long pressure and shortages
episodes.place: Rome; Procopius' relevant account is Wars VII / Gothic War III, §§36–40, with entry via a gate and Rome's garrison surrendering/withdrawing

sources.kind: primary narrative, Procopius, Gothic War III, §§1–7
sources.access: Full page accessed
sources.locator: Page title explicitly covers Gothic Wars III.1–7
sources.supports: This linked page does not contain the capture account cited by the episode; it is a source pointer mismatch for the capture event.

sources.kind: primary narrative, Procopius, Gothic War III, §§36–40
sources.access: Search-result passage consulted; full page not opened
sources.locator: §36, esp. §7 in excerpt: Isaurian guards open negotiations with Totila and agree to surrender Rome
sources.supports: Search extract supports a negotiated/betrayed opening of the city after a prolonged siege.
sources.limits: Excerpt only. It does not independently substantiate the episode's broad population/civilian claims or exact effects of the capture.

sources.kind: archaeological site information portal quoting Procopius
sources.access: Search-result extract only
sources.locator: Gothic War VII, XV, 546 CE
sources.supports: Search extract discusses Portus garrison and harbour operations during the campaign.
sources.limits: Portal excerpt, not the primary text edition; not evidence for modern spatial precision.

episodes.assessment: The URL currently cited in the episode (7A) is wrong for the Rome capture; likely relevant Procopius passage is 7G / Gothic War III.36–40. Capture and surrender can be attributed to Procopius, while population figures/refuge details need separate sources.

episodes.date: 552 CE Narses retakes Rome; final Gothic resistance ends 553, war conventionally concludes 554
episodes.place: Rome; Taginae/Busta Gallorum and Mons Lactarius are distant campaign locations, not the Rome map location

sources.kind: primary narrative, Procopius, Wars VIII.33–35
sources.access: Full page opened and relevant passage read
sources.locator: VIII.33.8–27; VIII.35
sources.supports: Procopius says Narses marched on Rome after the battle, captured it in Justinian's 26th regnal year, and sent the keys to Justinian; later passage recounts the final Gothic resistance and negotiated departure.
sources.limits: Procopius' regnal dating is not a modern exact date; no single 553 victory alone establishes total and immediate control over all Italy. The broader war ended over several years.

sources.kind: primary narrative, Procopius, Wars VIII.29–32
sources.access: Full page opened; battle passage read
sources.locator: VIII.31, Narses/Totila battle at Taginae
sources.supports: Describes Narses' battle deployment and Totila's defeat/death.
sources.limits: Does not itself prove full territorial restoration; the exact battlefield location should not be reduced to modern coordinates.

episodes.assessment: The entry compresses retaking Rome (552), defeat of Totila at Taginae (552), final battle against Teias at Mons Lactarius (553), and war end (554). Keep dates/places distinct; Britannica is secondary, not a primary source.

episodes.date: 593–595 CE; entry's 590 is only a pontificate prologue
episodes.place: Rome and Lombard/imperial territories in Italy; Gregory writes to an official serving the Exarch

sources.kind: primary letter, Gregory the Great, Register V.36
sources.access: Full letter read
sources.locator: Register V.36, paragraphs 1–3
sources.supports: Gregory says Agilulf was willing to pursue general peace if the Exarch consented to arbitration over alleged violations during an existing peace; each side could seek satisfaction. Gregory warns that a separate peace with his own side might leave islands/other places ruined.
sources.limits: This is Gregory's advocacy to an intermediary, not proof that a peace treaty was concluded in 593 or universal religious consensus. The claim that Rome reached agreement requires later correspondence (e.g. Register IX.42) and qualified chronology.

sources.kind: primary letter, Gregory, Register IX.42
sources.access: Search-result text consulted, not full page in this audit
sources.locator: To Agilulf; asks his dukes to keep the peace already made
sources.supports: Later correspondence refers to a peace having been made and requests its observance.
sources.limits: Search excerpt only; distinguish this later confirmation from the initial negotiation letter V.36.

episodes.assessment: Current candidate blends negotiation (V.36) with later peace (IX.42); keep the shift and date qualified rather than treating the negotiation itself as completed peace.

episodes.date: 596 dispatch; mission arrives Britain/Kent in 597; later steps continue after these dates
episodes.place: Rome to Britain, then Thanet/Kent and Canterbury in Bede's account

sources.kind: primary letter, Gregory the Great, Register VI.51
sources.access: Full letter read
sources.locator: Book VI, Letter 51; dateline gives Mauricius regnal/indictional year
sources.supports: Gregory exhorts the departing mission to continue and obey Augustine, who is returning to them. Dated by the letter's indiction/regnal formula, commonly 596.
sources.limits: Letter is an instruction to missionaries; it does not independently record arrival in Kent or conversion outcomes.

sources.kind: later narrative chronology, Bede, Ecclesiastical History I.23, I.25, I.29
sources.access: Full chronology page read
sources.locator: Chronological table: 596 dispatch, 597 arrival, 601 additional clergy/pallium
sources.supports: Bede gives 596 as Gregory's dispatch, 597 for arrival, and 601 for further personnel and pallium.
sources.limits: Bede writes in the eighth century; narrative chapters I.23–26 include reported royal conversations, not contemporary transcripts. Mission was gradual; neither all England nor all Britons converted in one episode.

sources.kind: Fordham sourcebook hosting Gregory's letter to Mellitus (601)
sources.access: Search-result citation only; page open failed
sources.locator: Gregory, Ep. 76 (601), as identified by Fordham
sources.supports: Not counted as independently read support for the 596/597 episode.
sources.limits: This is a later instruction from 601, not the initial mission dispatch; full page was not accessible in this audit.

episodes.assessment: Mission dispatched by Gregory and arrival in 597 are supported by Gregory's letter plus Bede's later chronology. Avoid a single conversion event or factualizing Bede's reported speeches.

geographyAndLicensing.geography: No coordinates, modern map tiles, georeferenced route geometry, or image assets were verified. The source texts name cities/regions but rarely locate specific buildings precisely. For episode 3 distinguish Ravenna's named palace/Lauretum in a late narrative from a surveyed archaeological footprint; for the Gothic War keep distant battles off-map if the selected geography is Rome.
geographyAndLicensing.licensing: No geographic or image resource license for game reuse was established. Text availability is not a license for page illustrations, maps, or modern translations. Project Gutenberg editions may carry public-domain status for the hosted old translations, but no specific map/image asset was cleared. The University of Chicago/LacusCurtius pages contain page-specific copyright notes; verify the exact page notice before reuse. No source in these entries supplies a reusable licensed map layer.
geographyAndLicensing.access: Entries distinguish full passages from search snippets and failed page opens; snippets are not represented as full source consultation.

crossEpisodeCautions: Episode 08 cites Britannica, a secondary overview; Marcellinus Comes is later than 476 and expressly frames the event as the end of the western empire. Avoid treating that retrospective formulation as universal contemporary perception.
Episode 11's older Catholic Encyclopedia summary is not the primary formula; the consulted formula web transcription explicitly labels its English translation AI-assisted/OCR-derived.
Episode 12 relies on later papal biographies and modern institutional summaries; embassy motive, exact dispatch date, and prison conditions are mediated by sources.
Episode 15's cited Procopius URL 7A covers Gothic War III.1–7, while capture discussion appears in the 7G search result (III.36–40); source locator needs correction by the editor.
Episode 16 compresses distinct events of 552, 553 and 554; Narses taking Rome is 552, not evidence for a single decisive restoration in 553.
Episode 18's 596/597 labels correspond to different phases: Gregory's dispatch and Bede's reported arrival. Later mission efforts and Christianization continue beyond 597.
